name: module-fqn-prefix
body:
The module identity that prefixes a module's symbol FQNs. Every identity below is now rendered under a LANGUAGE ROOT: the ingestor prefixes the module identity with the scanned language's id and wires `Language —Contains→ Module` (requirements.requirement.language-rooting, requirements.requirement.language-rooted-module-fqn). The rendered Module FQN is `<language-id>.<module-identity>`, and symbols inherit it through `parent.name`. This is the namespace form that makes the shared Module namespace collision-free ACROSS languages by construction — two same-named modules/symbols in different languages live under disjoint roots (`rust.apg` vs `py.apg`), so the cross-language collisions the meanings below used to risk (and the ingestor's silent module shadowing of them) cannot occur. Within one language the collision handling is unchanged: module-vs-type shadowing (`shadowed_modules`) and the same-kind `claim` panic still apply (requirements.requirement.cross-language-collision-freedom). Several distinct meanings share the one Module namespace; each is the `<module-identity>` under its own language root.

(1) Discovered code projects — language/package-derived: a Cargo package name (root `apg` vs nested `apg-rustfrontend`) or an npm package name for JS/TS. Distinct prefixes keep nested-project FQNs disjoint (see requirements.requirement.rust-nested-fqn-clean). Rendered under the root: `rust.apg` / `rust.apg-rustfrontend`, `ts.@co/ui` / `js.some-pkg`.

(2) Markdown documents — path-derived: a markdown Module's FQN is `md.` + its directory's absolute path, and its File's FQN is the file's absolute path with the extension retained (`docs/README.md` and `docs/README.markdown` stay distinct). This is the pinned scheme (requirements.requirement.markdown-sections-as-symbols, requirements.requirement.markdown-accept-extensions), NOT the rejected dot-joined directory scheme, which is lossy (it aliases `docs/guide` and `docs.guide` to the same `docs.guide` prefix).

(3) Repo-root markdown directory — `md.` + the repo-root directory's absolute path. The root directory is itself a directory with an absolute path, so there is always a path to name it; this closes open point 5 of requirements.note.markdown-frontend-open-points, whose premise that the root directory offers no path to name it was wrong.

(4) Python packages — package-derived dotted identity: a directory with __init__.py/__init__.pyi is a package, and the dotted identity walks up init-bearing ancestors; a file with no init-bearing ancestor is a flat top-level module by stem (domain.entity.python-package, requirements.requirement.python-package-identity). Like (1) this is a language/package-derived identity, so it is NOT automatically disjoint from other languages' module names (a root Python package `apg` would collide with the Rust `apg` module, and two same-stem init-less top-level modules in different directories would alias). DECIDED — the language root resolves open point 1: the rendered Python Module FQN is `py.<dotted-identity>` (the language-namespaced form), disjoint from every other language's root and from markdown's rooted absolute paths, so python-package-identity's collision-freedom is delivered by construction (requirements.note.python-frontend-open-points #1 is DECIDED).

Collision hazard and resolution: path-derived identities now render as `md.<absolute-path>` and language/package-derived identities as `<language-id>.<identity>`, so the cross-language and the path-vs-package hazards are both removed by the disjoint language roots. Within markdown, absolute paths remain unique per directory and per file, so module/file prefixes stay disjoint; a POSIX absolute path begins with `/`, which no Cargo/npm/Go/Java package name does, so the rooted markdown Module can never collide with a rooted code module.
